title: Seed-once tenant loading with seedVersion
story: Tenant seeding must not overwrite console edits: boot re-puts every tenants/*.json so an admin-console change is lost on restart.
acceptance: loadDir() puts a tenants/*.json file only when the tenant has no stored config, or when the file's top-level seedVersion (missing = 0) is greater than the stored config's seedVersion (missing = 0)
A tenant whose stored config was changed via put() (e.g. console edit) is NOT overwritten on a later loadDir() when the file seedVersion is not greater; a higher file seedVersion does overwrite

loadDir() logs per tenant whether it was applied (new / seedVersion upgrade) or skipped (kept stored config), and still returns the list of tenant ids present (applied or skipped) so existing callers keep working
docs/setup.md documents seed-once semantics, the seedVersion field, how to force a re-seed by bumping it, and that npm run demo:reset wipes data/ and therefore reseeds from files

New tests in tests/unit/core/tenants.test.mjs cover: first boot, restart with console edit preserved, seedVersion bump applied, missing seedVersion treated as 0, invalid file still rejected; run: node --test --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning tests/unit/core/tenants.test.mjs
All existing core tests stay green (tests/unit/core/*.test.mjs that touch tenants, e.g. server.test.mjs, tenant-context.test.mjs)
brief: Edit loadDir() in src/core/tenants.mjs (about line 73). For each file: parse JSON, id = config.id ?? basename. Read stored = latest(id). Decide: apply if no stored row; else apply if Number(config.seedVersion ?? 0) > Number(parse(stored.config).seedVersion ?? 0); else skip. Use db.parseJson(stored.config). Apply via api.put(id, config, 'boot'); put already no-ops when identical, so a bump with identical content is fine. Log with ctx.log if present (check src/core/log.mjs and core-runtime-api.md for the logger shape; guard with optional chaining since loadDir may run before the logger is wired in tests), e.g. 'tenant seed applied' / 'tenant seed skipped' with {tenantId, reason, fileSeedVersion, storedSeedVersion}. Do not log config contents. Keep returning all ids. A console edit that goes through put() keeps the stored config's seedVersion only if the editor preserves the field; if an edit drops it, stored is treated as 0, so a file with seedVersion >= 1 would re-apply: document this and note that console edits should carry seedVersion forward (do not change other files; if the admin console strips it, post a note to the architecture hub with node org/cli.mjs post architecture contract-change). Do not add seedVersion to tenants/*.json (not your paths; absent equals 0 and that is fine) and do not edit package.json. Tests: build ctx via the helper in tests/unit/core/helpers.mjs, write temp tenants dir with os.tmpdir, create tenants twice over the same DB to simulate restart. Validators: register none or a minimal one; check how existing tests construct createTenants. Only write your three paths; run only your test file plus the core tests that touch tenants.
valueDrivers: Safe, explicit config upgrades for licensed insurers
